title: Linear vs Jira: Which Issue Tracker Fits Your Team?
description: Linear vs Jira for software teams: compare issue tracking, sprint workflows, customization, integrations, reporting, administration, and total cost. Use your own backlog to test which workflow fits.

features.name: Core workflow
features.tool1: Issue tracking with opinionated, streamlined workflows
features.tool2: Issue tracking with configurable project and workflow models
features.tool1Detail: Test whether Linear's default workflow maps to your team's issue states, triage, and release process without extensive customization.
features.tool2Detail: Test how Jira projects, issue types, and workflows map to your team's process; advanced configuration may require an administrator.

features.name: Sprint and backlog planning
features.tool1: Supports planning workflows; verify fit for your process
features.tool2: Supports configurable agile boards and sprint workflows
features.tool1Detail: Run a real sprint with estimation, prioritization, cycle planning, and reporting, then verify which plan includes the capabilities you need.
features.tool2Detail: Run the same sprint and confirm board configuration, backlog behavior, permissions, and reporting in the Jira plan you would buy.

features.name: Workflow customization
features.tool2: Broad project and workflow configuration options
features.tool1Detail: Check whether available workflow states and team settings cover your process before migrating.
features.tool2Detail: Check the configuration effort needed for issue types, fields, workflows, and permissions; complex setups need governance.

features.name: Developer workflow
features.tool1: Designed around product and engineering teams
features.tool2: Supports software teams and wider Jira project use cases
features.tool1Detail: Test issue-to-code links, pull-request updates, triage, and the development tools your team uses.
features.tool2Detail: Test issue-to-code links, development integrations, and whether your team needs Jira Software-specific capabilities or other Atlassian products.

features.name: Integrations
features.tool1: Integration availability depends on the services and plan
features.tool2: Broad ecosystem; specific integrations and capabilities vary
features.tool1Detail: Verify each required integration and test the exact events and fields exchanged.
features.tool2Detail: Verify whether the integration is native, marketplace-based, or requires another Atlassian product or paid add-on.

features.name: Automation
features.tool1: Verify available automation and usage limits for your plan
features.tool1Detail: Test triggers, actions, permissions, and usage limits against your real workflow.
features.tool2Detail: Check rule limits and execution quotas on the intended plan, and test how failed or repeated actions are handled.

features.name: Reporting
features.tool1: Evaluate built-in views and reports against team needs
features.tool2: Reporting options depend on project setup and plan
features.tool1Detail: Confirm that cycle, project, and team-level views answer the questions your leads need to ask.
features.tool2Detail: Confirm that sprint, issue, and project reports cover your metrics without requiring an add-on or manual export.

features.name: Administration and access
features.tool1: Check role, team, and organization controls for your plan
features.tool2: Check project permissions and organization-level administration for your plan
features.tool1Detail: Ask the vendor to confirm SSO, provisioning, audit, and access-control requirements for the exact plan under consideration.
features.tool2Detail: Ask the vendor to confirm SSO, provisioning, audit, and access-control requirements for the exact plan under consideration.

features.name: Migration and exports
features.tool1: Validate imports, exports, attachments, and issue relationships before moving
features.tool2: Validate imports, exports, attachments, issue relationships, and project configuration before moving
features.tool1Detail: Run a sample migration and compare issue history, relationships, comments, attachments, and user mapping.
features.tool2Detail: Run a sample migration and compare issue history, relationships, comments, attachments, and user mapping.

features.name: Pricing and total cost
features.tool1: Check current per-user pricing, billing terms, and plan limits
features.tool2: Check current per-user pricing, billing terms, plan limits, and any marketplace apps
features.tool1Detail: Use Linear's official pricing page and calculate annual cost for the required seats and features: https://linear.app/pricing.
features.tool2Detail: Use Atlassian's official pricing page and calculate annual cost for the required seats, products, and marketplace apps: https://www.atlassian.com/software/jira/pricing.

verdict: Linear and Jira can both support software issue tracking, but the better fit depends on how much structure and customization your team needs. Start with Linear if your team prefers a focused product-development workflow and wants to test whether its built-in conventions cover the work. Start with Jira if you need configurable issue types, project workflows, or an established Atlassian environment. These are evaluation starting points, not a universal ranking. Recreate a representative sprint in both tools, verify integrations and administration requirements on the intended plans, and compare annual cost plus migration and maintenance effort.

faqs.question: What is the main difference between Linear and Jira?
faqs.answer: Both can organize software work, issues, and team workflows. Linear emphasizes a focused product-development experience; Jira offers extensive configuration across issue types, projects, and workflows. The practical difference depends on the conventions your team wants to adopt and how much customization it needs.

faqs.question: Which is better for a startup?
faqs.answer: Neither is best for every startup. Test Linear if your team wants a streamlined engineering workflow with minimal configuration. Test Jira if you need specific issue types, custom workflows, or already rely on Atlassian tools. Make the decision after running the same sprint and triage process in both.

faqs.question: Which costs less?
faqs.answer: The answer depends on seat count, billing term, plan features, and any Jira marketplace apps or related products. Check the current official pricing pages at https://linear.app/pricing and https://www.atlassian.com/software/jira/pricing, then calculate the annual cost for the exact configuration you need.

faqs.question: Can we migrate from Jira to Linear or from Linear to Jira?
faqs.answer: A migration should be tested before committing. Check which issue fields, comments, attachments, relationships, project settings, and history can be transferred, and identify what needs manual cleanup. Import/export options and limitations can change, so confirm the current migration path with the vendors.

faqs.question: Which has better reporting and automation?
faqs.answer: Do not assume that a feature label means both products provide the same capability. List the reports and automations your team actually uses, then test triggers, limits, permissions, and outputs on the intended plan. Include any paid add-ons in the cost comparison.

faqs.question: What should we test before choosing?
faqs.answer: Use a real but non-critical project. Run triage, sprint planning, issue-to-code linking, automation, reporting, access controls, and an export or migration sample. Record setup effort, ongoing administration, missing features, and total annual cost before making a decision.
